entries.what_happened: Two OpenAI manuscripts, each claiming a negative answer to Zariski's question whether embedded topology determines multiplicity for complex hypersurface germs. (1) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three' (dated 24 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there is a finite N > 3 divisible by eight (the text gives N = 4s₀ + 16, where s₀ is the variable count of two seed polynomials fixed by an integer relation it does not evaluate) and two reduced polynomials f₁, f₂ with real coefficients, weighted homogeneous for positive rational weights, each with an isolated critical point at the origin, with ord₀f₁ = 2, ord₀f₂ = 3, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂᴺ, V(f₁), 0) ≅ (ℂᴺ, V(f₂), 0). The construction builds sums of chain singularities from an integer relation among rational weights, matches the spectra modulo 2, obtains an integral Seifert-form isometry (Steenbrink/Némethi and Hertling–Mase/Orlik–Randell for the separate real and integral identifications, then a single integral isometry by strong approximation), applies Levine's classification of simple spherical knots, and extends the link equivalence to an ambient homeomorphism by a weighted cone map. Corollaries in the same manuscript (outside this problem's scope): f₁ and f₂ are topologically right equivalent, Arnold's Hessian-corank question is answered negatively, and initial-form Milnor fibres differ after adding t². (2) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five' (dated 27 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there are reduced convergent holomorphic germs f₄, f₅ : (ℂ⁴, 0) → (ℂ, 0), each with an isolated critical point at 0, with ord₀f₄ = 4, ord₀f₅ = 5, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂ⁴, V(f₄), 0) ≅ (ℂ⁴, V(f₅), 0). The construction starts from the plane curve h = T(X − T²)(X − 2T²) and two degree-four finite graph maps π₀, π₁, whose pullbacks are plane curves of the same embedded type with isometric integral Seifert forms. It smooths the cone yz = w⁴ and adds w(y^a + z^b) to h, with a and b given by formulas in an integer n₀ fixed by congruences. The integral Seifert congruence is obtained by strong approximation, the link equivalence by Kato's Theorem B on Milnor open books of S⁷, and the ambient homeomorphism by an analytic ambient-pair cone theorem (Massey, Theorem 1.4).
entries.delivers: For the pair form (two varieties at singular points that are topologically equivalent have equal multiplicity), both manuscripts claim a counterexample for complex hypersurface germs with isolated critical points: multiplicities 2 and 3 in ℂᴺ for some N > 3 divisible by eight (so N ≥ 8), and multiplicities 4 and 5 in ℂ⁴. An ambient homeomorphism of pairs carries V(f) onto V(g), so these pairs are topologically equivalent in the list's sense; the counterexample therefore reaches the list's pair form for reduced hypersurface germs. Both manuscripts describe the result as a negative answer to Zariski's embedded question (paper 1 calls it the 'embedded Zariski multiplicity conjecture'). The statement they prove is the classical hypersurface form, not the list's unrestricted 'varieties'. The family form (b) is not addressed: neither manuscript constructs a topologically equisingular family, and paper 1 says its pair cannot be joined by a μ-constant family and that arbitrary equivalent pairs do not reduce to the family problem.
entries.remains: (b) the family form, i.e. whether a topologically equisingular family of singular points has constant multiplicity, is not addressed by either manuscript. (c) Dimension three (ℂ³) is stated by both to remain untreated. Paper 1 does not cover N = 5, 6, 7 or N ≡ 0 mod 8 other than its unspecified N. Paper 2 is specific to N = 4. Plane curves (n = 2) are classically positive per paper 2's introduction (Zariski 1932), so the examples do not reach them. Non-hypersurface varieties, non-isolated singularities, and real or algebraic (non-holomorphic) varieties are not treated. Paper 1 says its construction is not intended to minimize the dimension.
entries.direction: disproves the pair form for complex hypersurface germs, in ℂ⁴ (multiplicities 4 and 5) and in ℂᴺ for some N ≥ 8 divisible by eight (multiplicities 2 and 3); the family form is untouched
entries.object: Paper 1: f₁, f₂ are explicit sums of chain polynomials and pure powers with all coefficients 1. Their weights come from an integer relation whose existence the text proves by a finite rank and adjugate computation, and a supplementary explicit relation with 849 nonzero integer coefficients is referenced (verification/support/explicit-relation.json, which I did not open). N is not computed. Paper 2: f₄, f₅ are not written out. They are given as h(p) + w(y^a + z^b) on the smooth fourfold yz = R_s(p,w), with a and b explicit functions of n₀, and then transferred to ℂ⁴ through analytic charts. The germs are constructed, not explicit power series.
entries.conditional_on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in either theorem; both rest on classical results invoked after their hypotheses are checked. Paper 1 relies on: Levine's classification of simple spherical knots; Thom–Sebastiani and Sakamoto's integral Seifert formula; Steenbrink, Némethi, Hertling–Mase and Orlik–Randell for the real and integral monodromy identifications; Eichler–Kneser–Platonov strong approximation (Rapinchuk, Theorem 2.3); King and Saeki for the right-equivalence corollary, with Sampaio's source-homeomorphism formulation; and Budur et al. (arXiv v3) for the initial-form corollary. Its finite seed relation is established by a computation, not a proof by hand. Paper 2 relies on: Milnor; Némethi's analytic form of Milnor's theorem; Kato's Theorem B (the text notes it needs no homotopy-sphere hypothesis on the binding, citing Kato p.454 and Durfee); Saeki; the analytic ambient-pair cone theorem (Massey, Theorem 1.4); and strong approximation (Platonov, Rapinchuk). Neither paper depends on the other for its proof; paper 2 says the two arguments are independent. The C³ companion (OpenAIMuConstant2026) is cited in paper 1 only in its family discussion, as far as I read.
entries.doubts: Paper 1: (i) the dimension N is not computed, so the claim is existential; the text says N 'is not intended to minimize' the dimension. (ii) The seed relation rests on finite calculations (a 1118-column cutoff matrix, rank over F₁₀₀₉, an adjugate of an 868-column minor), and the text says a supplied Python program checks them. The repository README says these checks 'cover the finite arithmetic, not the lattice-theoretic or topological arguments'. I did not open or run the programs. (iii) The abstract's topological right equivalence is a corollary, not part of Theorem 1.1, and the source homeomorphism is 'not claimed to be holomorphic or bi-Lipschitz' and need not coincide with the ambient map. (iv) Several results are cited to literature versions, e.g. 'arXiv v3' for Budur et al. Paper 2: (i) the authors flag a limit on a step: 'we do not assert that h is submersive through every value in the disk at θ = 0'; sublevel totals are then isotoped as manifolds with corners. (ii) Thresholds are stated as 'sufficiently large' a, b and 'sufficiently small' s, without numerical bounds; the existence of admissible parameters is a congruence construction. (iii) No computer verification accompanies this paper, and its folder has no verification directory. (iv) Kato's Theorem B is applied to bindings that need not be homotopy spheres; the text cites it rather than re-proving it. (v) I read the statements and the flagged passages of its nine sections, not every proof.
